reasoning_traces.think:
The Generalized Matching Equation (GME) operates as a stochastic choice rule linking reinforcement magnitude R_i to behavioral frequency B_i through a power-law transformation controlled by discrimination parameter α. When applied to NFL play-calling, it models how teams distribute play types based on past reinforcement (yards gained). By substituting yards gained with success rate (SR), the model shifts from outcome-based to efficacy-based reinforcement, improving predictive accuracy. The behavioral choice kernel K_ij(t) emerges as a normalized weighted transition matrix that reflects the influence of SR-derived rewards on strategic decisions. This kernel enables GSE to simulate dynamic play-calling policies, while GSI uses its probabilistic structure to infer team tendencies and adjust forecasts. Dualities arise between SR and yards-gained as reinforcement measures, with SR offering superior generalization due to its contextual normalization. Failure modes occur when environmental drift disrupts stable reinforcement schedules or when behavioral repertoire expands beyond modeled actions.
